GRIEVANCE XX ◆ MORAL OBLIGATION

He has diminished the nation’s pursuit of knowledge, making scientific inquiry vulnerable to political favor.

THE RECORD SHOWS

Grant cancellations, proposed funding cuts, and political pressure on research have disrupted U.S. science and prompted researchers to leave.

A federal appeals court held that the administration could not impose a steep NIH indirect-cost cap. Associated Press reporting traced a broader loss of scientists and uncertain funding. The White House says it is reducing waste and prioritizing research it considers valuable.

A DOCUMENTED SEQUENCE

3 MILESTONES
  1. 2025The administration attempted broad cancellations and restrictions on scientific grants and federal research institutions.
  2. January 2026An appeals court rejected a sharp cap on National Institutes of Health indirect-cost reimbursements.
  3. October 2026Associated Press interviewed researchers who had left, or were leaving, U.S. institutions amid cuts and political uncertainty.

WHAT THE RECORD DOES NOT ESTABLISH

Researchers’ decisions to relocate have multiple causes. The cited interviews document individual experiences, not an exact count of scientists driven abroad by the administration.
